policy: Human-curated paraphrases from university extension and public IPM guidance. No page content is scraped at scan time. Chemical product, rate, and timing instructions are deliberately excluded.

entries.title: Apple scab: reduce carry-over and leaf wetness
entries.summary: Apple scab management starts with sanitation and practices that help leaves and fruit dry more quickly.
actions: Remove or break down fallen infected leaves after the season.
Prune to improve air movement and sunlight through the canopy.
Avoid overhead irrigation where practical and consider locally suitable resistant varieties.
entries.region_scope: New England guidance; cultural principles are broadly relevant, but varieties and pesticide decisions must be confirmed locally.

entries.title: Corn common rust: start with resistant hybrids
entries.summary: Common rust often remains below damaging levels, and resistant corn hybrids are the main management measure.
actions: Compare pustules on both leaf surfaces with local common-rust guidance before acting.
Choose resistant hybrids when common rust is a recurring local problem.
Ask a local crop adviser whether disease pressure and crop stage justify any further action.
entries.region_scope: Upper Midwestern United States; disease pressure and hybrid recommendations vary by region.

entries.title: Grape black rot: sanitation and canopy drying
entries.summary: Removing infected material and helping the canopy dry can reduce sources and conditions that favor grape black rot.
actions: Remove diseased material and black, shriveled fruit left on vines or the ground.
Use pruning, training, and spacing to promote canopy drying.
Confirm any preventive spray program with current local grape guidance before use.
entries.source_name: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach
entries.region_scope: Iowa and similar production settings; pesticide registration and timing are location-specific.

entries.title: Potato early blight: maintain crop vigor
entries.summary: Early blight risk can be reduced by maintaining suitable crop nutrition and irrigation and by limiting infected potato refuse between crops.
actions: Review fertility, irrigation, and other stresses that may be reducing crop vigor.
Reduce infected potato refuse and rotate crops where locally appropriate.
Confirm the diagnosis and any fungicide decision with current local potato guidance.
entries.source_name: University of California Statewide Integrated Pest Management Program
entries.region_scope: California production guidance; local climate, resistance, registration, and timing may differ.

entries.title: Late blight: confirm quickly and keep foliage dry
entries.summary: Late blight can spread quickly in cool, wet conditions, so suspected cases need prompt confirmation and nearby crops may also be at risk.
actions: Keep foliage dry where practical and inspect nearby tomato and potato plants.
Do not move or compost suspect infected material before obtaining local disposal guidance.
Contact a local extension service or plant clinic promptly for confirmation and region-specific management.
entries.region_scope: Minnesota garden and farm guidance; outbreak status and permitted products vary by region.

entries.title: Bean anthracnose: clean seed and moisture management
entries.summary: Bean anthracnose can move with infected seed, debris, splashing rain, irrigation water, and field activity under cool, moist conditions.
actions: Use certified disease-free seed and resistant varieties when available.
Avoid overhead irrigation where practical and avoid working wet plants.
Manage infected debris and plan a locally suitable non-bean rotation.
entries.source_name: University of California Statewide Integrated Pest Management Program
entries.region_scope: California dry-bean guidance; rotation length, cultivars, and production practices require local confirmation.

entries.title: Bean rust: airflow and splash reduction
entries.summary: Spacing, reduced leaf wetness, removal of infected material, and resistant varieties can help limit bean rust.
actions: Space plants to support air circulation and avoid overhead sprinklers where practical.
Remove infected leaves and shoots without spreading debris through the crop.
Check locally adapted resistant varieties and seek local advice before considering a pesticide.
entries.source_name: University of California Statewide Integrated Pest Management Program
entries.region_scope: California home and landscape guidance; commercial management and pesticide registration require local confirmation.
